messages:
priya: noticing a small but persistent tail on shared-gpu-3 since ~08:10 UTC. p50 fine, p95 up ~60ms, p99 up ~250ms. correlates with a single tenant (ad-par1) ramping up long-seq requests.

jordan: ack. did you see kernel switches or batch size changes in the traces?

priya: grabbing traces now. initial look shows frequent kernel_autoswitch events and KV cache eviction spikes for that GPU host. stack traces attached in prod trace (link).

mike: can you paste the prom query for the kv evictions? I want to grep logs.

priya: sure: ``rate(runtime_kv_evictions_total{pool="shared-gpu-3"}[1m])`` showed a 4x jump starting 08:09. also: ``histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{pool="shared-gpu-3"}[2m])) by (le))`` for p99.

jordan: interesting — kernel selection logic flips to an FP16-quant path at ~512 tokens, but that path uses a different KV slot layout which seems to cause higher eviction churn when many long sequences interleave. looks like the tenant's workload has a long-tail of sequence lengths that triggers frequent kernel swaps.

elaine: any obvious noisy-tenant signature? like sustained QPS or a few huge batches?

priya: it's mostly lots of small concurrent requests plus intermittent 2–3 long seqs (2k+). concurrency pattern leads to alternating kernel decisions: short-path vs long-path. each flip invalidates some prefetched KV regions -> eviction thrash.

mike: running an esi profile now (`/opt/profiler run --pool shared-gpu-3 --window 5m`) — will post results in 2 mins.

infra-bot: deploy is queued: rollback/patch/kv-pin @priya requested. CI:green.

priya: mitigation ideas: 1) temp rate-limit ad-par1 at pool level (cap concurrent long-seq to 2) 2) force kernel policy to prefer long-path for requests >1024 tokens (avoid oscillo) 3) enable per-tenant KV pinning for hot prefixes. prefer 1+2 short-term.

jordan: +1. I can push a pool-level per-tenant concurrency cap via config: ``/api/v1/pools/shared-gpu-3/tenants/ad-par1/limits`` -> set concurrent_longseq:2. I'll stage a change now.

mike: profiler results: flamegraph shows 48% time in kernel_reload + 22% in kv_reclaim calls during spike window. attached snippet: ``kernel_reload() -> select_kernel_variant() -> kv_reclaim_if_needed()`` repetitive loop.

priya: that matches. also seeing bursty batching heuristic flips: when the scheduler tries to maximize throughput it grows batch_size which nudges kernel decision. need a hysteresis in batch-size growth.

elaine: can we short-circuit by preferring stable kernel choice per-connection for N requests? like sticky kernel decision for 30s unless explicit signal.

jordan: yes, implement sticky kernel affinity TTL=30s would reduce oscillation. I'll prototype a config flag `kernel.affinity_ttl_sec`. low-risk patch.

priya: implementing caps now + asking SRE to throttle ad-par1 to reduce immediate impact. after that we can deploy kernel.affinity_ttl_sec=30 and maybe increase KV slot tolerance.

infra-bot: change applied: pool limit updated (ad-par1 concurrent_longseq=2) by jordan at 08:25 UTC.

mike: after the cap, p99 dropped from +250ms to +40ms in the last 5m. KV eviction rate down 6x.

elaine: great. can we add an alert rule to detect kernel flip rate? e.g., ``rate(kernel_autoswitch_total[1m]) > 5`` per GPU -> ops page.

jordan: on it. also opening a follow-up to consider per-tenant kernel pinning for predictable workloads and a batching hysteresis heuristic in the scheduler.

priya: filing a post-incident ticket with logs, traces, profiler graphs, and proposed mitigations (kernel affinity TTL, batching hysteresis, KV pin API). tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform.

mike: note for postmortem: this is an emergent interaction between batching heuristic + kernel selection + KV layout mismatch — not just a noisy QPS. archival note: workload with mixed short/long seqs is high-risk on shared pools.

elaine: thanks team — monitoring for 30m. reopen if we see regression. :thumbsup:
